data.title: Estée Lauder CEO praises travel retail, online sales as Q1 net sales grow 6%
data.description:
The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. reported increases in online sales in Asia and in its travel retail business during the company’s fiscal first quarter ended Sept. 30.

The Health & Beauty brand raised its outlook for fiscal 2027, citing improved profitability in Q1 as net sales grew 6.7% year over year to $3.7 billion.

Estée Lauder is No. 42 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Estée Lauder is also No. 310 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Why Estée Lauder raised its outlook for 2027

“The energy and determination of our teams, combined with the strength of our brands and the progress of our transformation, give me greater confidence than ever in the opportunities that lie ahead,” said Stéphane de La Faverie, president and CEO at Estée Lauder. “We are raising our fiscal 2027 outlook, reflecting both our strong start and our conviction in the future we are creating.”

The company now expects to see organic net sales growth of 4.0% to 5.5% instead of its previously forecast 3% to 5% in its full 2027 fiscal year.

In its earnings release, Estée Lauder credited what it characterized as “strong performance in the fiscal 2027 first quarter,” even as it stayed “cautious amid ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty.”

Highlights for the quarter included expanded availability through online channels, as well as successes in Asia and travel retail.

Where Estée Lauder online sales grew in Q1

Estée Lauder reported that it widened online consumer availability of its products on Amazon, where the company claimed to now have 13 brands across 17 markets. In the meantime, it also expanded to 15 brands present across 11 markets on TikTok Shop.

Its online sales encompass direct sales from its individual brands and retailers’ ecommerce sites, as well as through third-party platforms.

Specifically, the company noted online sales growth in Asia, where its new fulfillment center in China’s Hainan province opened in July, as well as in its travel retail business division.

“We delivered high-single-digit organic sales growth online [in Q1], driven by both established platform and expansion,” said de La Faverie on an earnings call with investors. “Encouragingly, online growth was also well balanced.”

He characterized growth broadly across regions.

“Asia Pacific rose double digit, while each of the other three regions grew high-single digits,” he stated. “In the U.S. and China, we gained share online with retail sales growth more than 2x faster than the industry in our two biggest markets.”

Estée Lauder’s investments in digital infrastructure

Estée Lauder, which uses Shopify as an ecommerce platform, extended use for M·A·C and Clinique brands’ sites in the U.S. and U.K. over the past quarter, as M·A·C physical stores also opened up in those markets.

Continued modernizing its digital technology infrastructure to deliver best-in-class consumer experiences with the full deployment of Shopify for M·A·C and Clinique on their US and UK brand.com, as well as the initial rollout for M·A·C freestanding stores in the US and UK.

In addition, Akhil Shrivastava, the chief financial officer at Estée Lauder, credited Shopify as a part of the company’s digital efforts, enabling what he called “superior consumer experiences, greater speed, simpler processes and improved productivity.”

“This can be seen in our Shopify deployment and the partnering with Profound, an AI marketing platform, bringing global insights into how our brands appear across AI platforms,” he stated.

data.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
data.description:
DoorDash Inc. announced a deal to acquire its last-mile delivery rival Instacart in a deal valued at $17 billion.

The combined company would unite operations from two of the most active platforms in retail and grocery delivery services through a transaction subject to approval by regulators and Instacart shareholders. DoorDash expects to use a combination of cash, stock and debt to finance the deal. As a result, the acquisition would enable DoorDash to leverage Instacart’s technology and expertise.

Why DoorDash is acquiring Instacart

“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” said Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, in the acquisition announcement. “Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts.”

Xu praised the work that Instacart has done to date.

“Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day,” he stated. “Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local.”

Online grocery sales in the U.S. grew by more than 20% year over year, increasing their share of total grocery spending, according to data tracked by the firm Brick Meets Click.

What comes next for Instacart

DoorDash and Instacart expect the deal to close near the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, the companies disclosed. After that, DoorDash expects to preserve the Instacart brand, along with its enterprise technology products and app. In the meantime, Instacart intends to continue to operate independently.

“Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Chris Rogers, CEO of Instacart. “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders.”

In the announcement, DoorDash noted that it could make 50,000 additional stores available to Instacart users through the deal, adding to almost 100,000 stores that already participate on Instacart’s platform.

data.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy in push to broaden audio brand portfolio
data.description:
Bose Corporation reached a deal to acquire fellow headphones brand Skullcandy, the companies formally announced on Oct. 21. The acquisition brings together two big names in consumer electronics and audio wearables, following a history of collaboration.

data.title: Bark revenue falls despite commerce growth resuming in Q2
data.description:
Bark net revenue and direct-to-consumer (DTC) revenue both declined in the company’s fiscal second quarter ended Sept. 30. However, the seller of pet products managed to reignite growth for its commerce revenue — which comes from sales with retail partners — and prepare the sale of its dog-focused airline as it sought to correct course for its business.

Overall, net revenue fell 18.1% year over year to $87.6 million in Q2, weighed down by reduced subscriber activity in its DTC sales.

Bark is No. 261 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Bark is also No. 806 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Bark web sales by year

Bark revenue in Q2

“Commerce returned to growth, Subscriber Retention improved to 94%, and we put our marketing dollars to work where they were most efficient,” said Matt Meeker, co-founder and CEO at Bark. “We also made meaningful progress expanding our product offerings and retail presence, including the launch of Licksters, our new line of enrichment toys, and the shipment of two of the largest retail orders in Bark’s history during our fiscal third quarter.”

Commerce net revenue in Q2 increased 3.6% from a year ago to reach $25.7 million. Meanwhile, DTC revenue declined 24.7% to $61.8 million over the same period.

Meeker addressed key challenges that have hindered growth at Bark in recent years. As he did so, he laid out Bark’s timeline for getting rid of its Bark Air, the dog airline service that launched in May 2024.

Selling Bark Air

“Subsequent to quarter end, we reached a preliminary understanding to sell Bark Air’s assets and license the brand beginning January 1, 2027,” Meeker stated. “The arrangement remains subject to definitive documentation and there is no assurance it will be completed.’

Assuming the deal goes through, Meeker expects Bark to be able to redirect funds toward its commerce operations, partnerships, supply chain and innovation efforts.

Bark Air originally debuted with service to New York, Los Angeles and London, later expanding to Paris, Lisbon, Madrid, Seattle, South Florida and San Francisco. The service eyed dogs and their human companions, offering specialized accommodations for them to travel together in the air. In addition, Bark Air offers a Companion Concierge service for travel planning, handling commercial and private flights, as well as ground transportation.

data.title: Walmart commits $6 billion to Symbotic for its AI and robotics solutions
data.description:
Walmart Inc.’s strategic investment, which accompanied Symbotic Inc.’s acquisition of Walmart’s robotics business, will grow by $6 billion, the companies announced on Oct. 29.

The new expansion of their commercial agreement will mean that new deployments of Symbotic’s automation technology appear at 25 of Walmart’s U.S. regional distribution centers, according to Symbotic. Added capabilities that Symbotic expects to roll out for Walmart’s global operations include means to support ecommerce upstream inventory management, increasing storage capacity and improving flow of products through the supply chain.

Walmart ranks No. 2 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database, which tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Walmart is also No. 37 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Why Walmart is investing more in Symbotic’s technology

“At Walmart, we’re focused on bringing more items to more customers and members, faster than ever,” said Rob Montgomery, executive vice president for Walmart U.S. supply chain operations. “Our investments in the physical and digital supply chain help us serve them however they choose to shop, whether in stores, at the curbside or at home.”

After more than a decade of working together and ultimately bringing Symbotic into Walmart fulfillment centers, the retail giant now sees success to build upon. That buildout will directly impact fulfillment for Walmart’s online sales.

“Our work with Symbotic over the years, including this expanded agreement, helps us improve service, grow capacity, simplify work for our associates and lower costs,” Montgomery stated.

What Symbotic does for Walmart

Symbotic provides solutions including BreakPack for handling small orders and mixed inventory, as well as SymMicro for micro-fulfillment with ecommerce orders. It also maintains software for operating those systems.

“Our partnership with Walmart started with a single product over a decade ago, and now we offer a full end-to-end solution to help power Walmart’s growth across its supply chain for years to come,” said Rick Cohen, chairman and CEO of Symbotic. “This expanded agreement reflects the strength of that collaboration — a partnership defined by trust and shared ambition.”

In a Securities and Exchange Commission filing dated Oct. 29, Symbotic outlines that Walmart would also work with the technology provider on a development program, with Walmart committing $125 million “to fund the research and development of next-generation racking technology and related picking, process flow and inventory management capabilities.”
